report.summary: Read daedalus/mapping/drift.py chunk 1/6: module docstring policy, constants, and class lists; enumerated claims vs visible code.
risks: drift.py:1-212 | medium | Module docstring makes many policy claims (single-engine, three unreached lists, acceptance tiers, snapshot digest, ignore config, first-run failure) that cannot be verified from this chunk alone; downstream readers may rely on them before seeing the implementation. | Read chunks 2-6 and verify each claim against the code.

drift.py:190-198 | low | ISLAND_CLASSES/UNKNOWN_CLASSES/SHIM_CLASSES and REACHED_CLASSES are defined but their coverage of reach.CLASSES is only asserted in tests not present here. | Check the test file for the coverage assertion.
drift.py:200-202 | low | DOC_DIRS/DOC_SUFFIX/DOC_EXTRA_FILES are declared but no parsing logic is visible in this chunk; the documented rule may be implemented later. | Verify in later chunks.
drift.py:206-209 | low | GENERATED_DOCS and _GENERATED_MARK are defined but their use in the documentation rule is not visible in this chunk. | Verify in later chunks.
drift.py:210-212 | low | MIN_DOC_DESC_CHARS and _ALNUM_RUN are defined but the description rule is not yet applied in this chunk. | Verify in later chunks.
todos: Read chunks 2-6 to verify the module docstring's claims about the implementation.
Confirm that UNREACHED_CLASSES and REACHED_CLASSES together cover reach.CLASSES (likely via tests).
Check that the documentation rule uses GENERATED_DOCS, _GENERATED_MARK, _FENCE_RE, MIN_DOC_DESC_CHARS, and _ALNUM_RUN as described.
Verify that the acceptance mechanisms (tiers, dates, stale acceptance) are implemented as documented.
Verify that the snapshot digest and coherence checks are implemented as documented.
Verify that the ignore configuration (IGNORE_FILENAME, IGNORE_ENV) is recorded and compared in the snapshot.
Verify that missing snapshot causes non-zero exit for both entry points.

claims.text: This module compares the CURRENT generated state against a COMMITTED snapshot (docs/architecture-state.json) and fails when they disagree.
claims.why: The comparison logic is not in this chunk; only the constant SNAPSHOT_REL is defined.

claims.text: This module DERIVES NOTHING ITSELF. Islands come from reach.analyse; switches come from switches.analyse; both are the same reports the page renders, computed once and passed in.
claims.why: No function bodies are present in this chunk; imports of reach_mod and switches_mod are listed but not shown.

claims.text: UNREACHED = every reach class that means "no entry point gets here", UNREACHED_CLASSES, split across THREE lists because the remedies are three different sentences
claims.why: The constants ISLAND_CLASSES, UNKNOWN_CLASSES, SHIM_CLASSES, and UNREACHED_CLASSES are defined and split into three categories.

claims.text: ``islands`` reach's ``island`` + ``orphan``. Those two are merged because the remedy really is identical
claims.why: ISLAND_CLASSES = ("island", "orphan") on line 190.

claims.text: ``unknown`` reach could not tell.
claims.why: UNKNOWN_CLASSES = ("unknown",) on line 195.

claims.text: ``shims`` a re-export nothing reaches.
claims.why: SHIM_CLASSES = ("shim",) on line 198.

claims.text: These three used to be one list containing only the first, and the other two were dropped on the floor
claims.why: Historical claim about previous versions; not verifiable from current code.

claims.text: Every unreached module is now counted, in exactly one of the three lists, and counts['unreached'] is their total
claims.why: The counting logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: the three lists together are a function of reach's classification and can only drift from it if UNREACHED_CLASSES stops covering a class reach can emit.
claims.why: The constants define the union of unreached classes; the comment on REACHED_CLASSES asserts the coverage property is tested.

claims.text: DARK = switches' ``dark`` verdict, MINUS the ones it classifies ``secret``, MINUS the ones documented BY THIS FILE'S RULE
claims.why: The dark calculation is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Darkness itself -- off by default, no fallback, in a boolean position -- is decided in exactly one place, switches
claims.why: The switches module is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A module reached only by its own test is STILL AN ISLAND here, and it is reported as one -- but under its own kind, TEST_ONLY, which does not block.
claims.why: TEST_ONLY is not defined in this chunk; no logic for test-only classification is visible.

claims.text: An environment variable that (a) is consumed as a BOOLEAN GATE, (b) defaults OFF with no fallback, and (c) is not documented.
claims.why: The dark switch definition is in switches module, not here.

claims.text: A switch counts as documented when, in a doc that is not generated and outside every fenced code block, it appears in a form an operator would actually type or an author would emphasise -- NAME=..., export NAME, set NAME, $env:NAME, "environment variable NAME", `NAME` or **NAME** -- and beside at least MIN_DOC_DESC_CHARS characters of other prose, on that line or the next non-empty one.
claims.why: The constants MIN_DOC_DESC_CHARS, GENERATED_DOCS, _GENERATED_MARK, and _FENCE_RE are present, and the docstring describes the rule; the actual parsing logic is not in this chunk, but the constants support the claim. However, the specific forms (NAME=..., export NAME, etc.) are not enumerated as constants in this chunk, so the full rule is uncheckable.

claims.text: Code fences are excluded because a fenced sample is where a name most often appears without being explained, and GENERATED_DOCS is excluded because daedalus map renders that file INTO the artifact this gate guards
claims.why: _FENCE_RE and GENERATED_DOCS are defined, and the docstring explains the exclusion. The actual implementation is not visible, but the constants match the claim.

claims.text: This is deliberately not "one designated inventory file with a description", which would be stronger still. It is not, because introducing that file is a documentation change outside this module, and a gate that fails until an unrelated file is created gets turned off rather than satisfied.
claims.why: This is a design rationale; no code to verify in this chunk.

claims.text: TIER 1 -- TEMPORARY, DATED, SELF-RESURFACING (acceptances in the snapshot)
claims.why: Acceptance mechanics are not in this chunk.

claims.text: EXPLICIT AND GREPPABLE -- grep -n 'island:' docs/architecture-state.json lists every island anyone is currently looking away from.
claims.why: Snapshot format not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: RECORDS WHY AND WHEN -- why under MIN_WHY_CHARS characters is rejected, and both dates are required.
claims.why: MIN_WHY_CHARS is defined on line 184; the validation logic is not in this chunk but the constant supports the claim.

claims.text: BOUND TO THE CALENDAR, NOT ONLY TO ITSELF. until is capped at MAX_HORIZON_DAYS past since AND since may not be in the future.
claims.why: MAX_HORIZON_DAYS is defined on line 182; the validation logic is not in this chunk but the constant supports the claim.

claims.text: Past until the acceptance stops suppressing and the underlying item comes back with the acceptance's own prose attached
claims.why: Resurfacing logic not in this chunk.

claims.text: An accepted item is NEVER written into the baseline (see write_snapshot).
claims.why: write_snapshot not in this chunk.

claims.text: An acceptance that matches nothing is a STALE ACCEPTANCE and blocks.
claims.why: Stale acceptance logic not in this chunk.

claims.text: TIER 2 -- PERMANENT, BY REVIEWED DIFF (--refresh). Deleting the acceptance and re-baselining moves the item into islands/dark_switches and bumps counts.
claims.why: Refresh logic not in this chunk.

claims.text: Every mechanical list is covered by a DIGEST_KEY over the canonical bytes, so hand-editing islands or dark_switches to pre-seed a finding into the baseline is an INVALID SNAPSHOT rather than a silent pass.
claims.why: Digest logic not in this chunk.

claims.text: The lists are additionally required to be internally coherent (islands, unknown and shims are subsets of modules; test_only is a subset of their union) and grounded in reality (dark_switches must name variables the code still reads).
claims.why: Coherence checks not in this chunk.

claims.text: every verb in this subsystem that READS a snapshot re-derives the digest first and refuses a mismatch. check reports INVALID SNAPSHOT.
claims.why: check function not in this chunk.

claims.text: render.accept -- which inherits the mechanical lists verbatim in order not to bank unrelated drift -- refuses to inherit them at all unless the digest it is inheriting verifies
claims.why: render.accept not in this chunk.

claims.text: refresh does not need the check: it rescans and overwrites every mechanical list from the tree.
claims.why: refresh function not in this chunk.

claims.text: DAEDALUS_IGNORE and .daedalusignore narrow the structural index. Since the gate now reads the tree through reach, which walks the filesystem itself, they cannot narrow what the gate sees -- but the configuration is recorded in the snapshot and compared on every run anyway
claims.why: IGNORE_FILENAME and IGNORE_ENV are defined on lines 200-201; the behavior claim is uncheckable but the constants exist.

claims.text: A missing snapshot is NOT a pass. Both entry points refuse it: daedalus map --check exits non-zero, and python -m daedalus.mapping.drift does too.
claims.why: Entry point behavior not in this chunk.

claims.text: Writing a baseline is an explicit named action (--init, --refresh, or a plain daedalus map), because rm docs/architecture-state.json must not be a way to get a green run.
claims.why: CLI actions not in this chunk.

claims.text: A full run parses every Python file in the tree twice (reachability and switches) and takes seconds, not milliseconds.
claims.why: Performance claim; no implementation in this chunk.

claims.text: Wired into pre-commit it would be bypassed with --no-verify within a week, and a gate people route around is worse than no gate because it also carries a claim of safety.
claims.why: Design rationale, no code to verify.
